installation.note: exit is a shell built-in (bash, sh, etc.)

overview.summary: exit terminates the current shell or script. With a numeric argument, it sets the exit status (0 = success, non-zero = failure). Without an argument, it uses the status of the last command. Typing exit in a login shell or terminal closes the session.
when_to_use: Close the current terminal or SSH session
Exit a script with a specific status (exit 1 on error)
End a subshell (exit in a script or after su)

syntax.description: N is the exit status (0-255). Exit the shell with that status; without N, use the last command's status.

examples.title: Close terminal
examples.description: Exit the current shell (close window or SSH session)

examples.title: Exit script with error
examples.use_case: In scripts: exit 1 after detecting an error

related_commands.description: Log out of login shell (similar to exit in login shell)
